schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE VOYAGE'S ANSWER, written after the build the chain charted. The chart chain ends at validate — what DONE would mean; this machine records what done ACTUALLY meant, criterion by criterion, and it is what the emit chokepoint and the build_inspector both read. It owns the DEPOSIT LEDGER (verdict-deposits.jsonl in instance-space): enqueue_verdict, pending, read_ledger, mark_deposited — one append door, and every reader goes through it.
why: IT IS A MACHINE BECAUSE IT HOLDS STATE, and that is the test rather than its size. A tool is a complete primitive and has USERS, not an owner (Akien, 2026-08-13) — because a tool holds nothing to gate. This module owns a durable append-only ledger, so there IS something to gate, so it needs an owner, so it is not a tool. It was nearly filed as a machine on line count; the ledger is the reason, and the reason is what the rung means. WHY THE RECORD AND NOT A COMPLAINT LIST (Akien, 2026-08-13): "passing such a thing without inspecting it means passing a mystery if something downstream fails … if every machine and even some more complex tools have their own inspector and gate, then each has documented and controllable quality validation … we can backtrack and see exactly where something went awry even if it's not something we're specifically looking for yet." A complaint list is empty both when every check passed and when no check ran, so the stage downstream is handed a mystery in exactly the case he named. The entries that PASSED are the ones nobody was looking for. "We might have to add more or better inspection questions, but that's fine. we learn as we go" — so the question list grows, and every addition is one more entry a reader sees whether it passed or failed.

feedback.why: MEASURED LINK: verdict requires validate_ref (verdict.py:109) and reads the obligations it renders judgment against through it, in both its forms — a validate packet or a ticket's own falsifier (verdict.py:240). Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. AND THIS STAGE IS WHERE HIS EXCEPTION WAS MEASURED, so it is recorded at the address it was measured at: askscan's five gaps ALL named verdict as the stage that ran last, and not one was verdict's to fix — three were ambiguities in the REQUEST and belonged above the whole chain. The declared route is still validate, because every_falsifier_clause_is_answered failing means the obligations verdict was handed could not be answered as written, and validate is the hand that wrote them. But the skip-level case is not hypothetical here and is not pretended away: on this stage it was the majority. The one-address shape cannot split a segment's findings by which side of its door they indict; see cairn/tools/feedback filed edge (e).

invoke: read by cairn/tools/base/transitions.py at the emit chokepoint and by the build_inspector; the inspector is inspect_verdict(artifact) and returns the proof record without taking a verdict, so a caller can READ what this stage proved without provoking its refusal
entry: Carved out of the chart machine on 2026-08-13 under Akien's ruling — "chart is a skill, it calls a collection of machines. that's the intention." The chart charter it was carved from is the design record of the whole chain and now berths with the skill at cairn/skills/chart/intention+why.json; this file holds only what is THIS component's.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, BORN AT THIS ADDRESS'S FIRST CROSSING. Until a ticket crosses here there is no journal, and that absence is this machine's ordinary resting state rather than a missing file — a component that has never sailed has no voyage to record. CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (ticket a-charter-may-not-assert-a-file-that-is-not-there): this sentence read 'Both were born at the carve-out', which was false — no journal has ever been born at a carve-out anywhere in the system. orient's arrived weeks after its carve-out, at its first crossing, and that is the mechanism for all eight. The fix is the sentence and never the files: an empty state.json here would manufacture a record of a voyage that did not happen (Law 7). The voyages that BUILT this stage before the carve-out are in the chart machine's history, which stays whole with the skill — a record of truth is never split. The LEDGER is runtime state and lives in instance-space, never here.
gates: VERDICT'S OWN INSPECTOR AND ITS OWN GATE, at this address (ruling 2026-08-13 every-machine-carries-its-own-inspector-and-gate). ``inspect_verdict`` returns a PROOF RECORD — shape, the required ticket claim, the claim's consistency, and coverage of every falsifier clause, each carrying EXPECTED beside ACTUAL — and ``validate_verdict`` is the == compare over it. THE REFUSAL IS THE FIRST MISMATCH, not all of them joined, and that is deliberate rather than inherited: these four checks are sequentially dependent (a malformed artifact cannot be asked about its claim), so a joined refusal would name derived failures as if they were independent findings. The record still holds every check that RAN, which is what makes the sequencing readable instead of merely obeyed. STAGE 8 HANDS ITS ARTIFACT TO NO NINTH STAGE and the ruling still lands here: the reader downstream of a verdict is a HUMAN reading the chain later, and an unrecorded pass is exactly as mysterious to them. The ledger's single append door (_append) is still the only writer, and mark_deposited is still the only thing that moves a row out of pending.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a second writer to the deposit ledger (Law 6 — one owner); (2) a verdict admitted with an unanswered criterion; (3) this module reaching tree machinery — the verdict path stays structurally unable to, and cairn/tools/import_sieve holds that as physics rather than as this sentence. (4) a check in this stage's inspector that PASSES SILENTLY — every check that ran appears in the record with its EXPECTED beside its ACTUAL, and a check that could not run is ABSENT rather than passed; (5) an oracle consulted anywhere on this path, at fire time or at sleep — `bin/cmd/determinism` must keep reading this component PURE DETERMINISTIC and REFUSES GATE.
horizon: re-read when the ledger grows a second consumer, or when a verdict face other than the per-claim one meets the embed ceiling.
how_it_learns: the per-claim deposit: one node per claim since 2026-07-29, so the metered embed seam takes the claim whole rather than a finished vector. The ledger is what makes a deposit resumable rather than lost when the embed seam is cold.
